title: THE CARD IN THE DRAWER · The stack
venue: the motel · a card left in room twelve's nightstand each month by a guest never seen · Box 12
logline: The sixth card, November: a tower struck by lightning. He redraws it as the mill's stack in 1994 with the whistle's jagged shape coming off its top instead of lightning, and two lunch pails falling. He had to invent the pails. He didn't know yet they'd be forty.

panels.composition: A single tall card filling the page, its border drawn as the wooden edge of a motel nightstand drawer; inside the border: a brick mill stack with a jagged whistle shape bursting from its top like lightning and two lunch pails falling past it, the yard below. No numeral, no title; the card's name is the thing.

image.notes: XVI, the Tower — the mill's stack and whistle (canon: The Mill, 1994, drawn ten years later). He invents the pails here first.
